title: Housekeeping items skip the Governance Poll but are fenced off from anything that changes risk
content:
A.1.11.1.5.1.2 opens a fast path: "Housekeeping items can be directly included in Executive Votes without a Governance Poll." Because that bypasses the sentiment gate entirely, the Atlas constrains it on two fronts.

The first is definitional. A.1.11.1.5.1.1 defines housekeeping items as "maintenance and record-keeping actions necessary to the correct functionality of the Sky Protocol" and then fences them by exclusion: they "do not include actions that modify risk parameters or introduce new elements into the protocol." Examples given are cleaning up technical debt, updating the Chainlog, and cancelling unused payment streams. Defining the category by what it excludes is what makes it non-expandable — anything touching risk or adding functionality is disqualified regardless of how routine it looks.

The second is procedural. The Core Facilitator must post the items and their rationale to the Forum, then "request a confirmation of the technical accuracy of the housekeeping items from the technical Ecosystem Actor (or Spell team) who is leading Spell development," who "must reply to the Forum Post confirming the accuracy." So the classification is attested by a second party, in public, before the item rides into an Executive.

A.1.11.1.5.1 adds a conflict-of-interest guard: where Spell teams propose the items, "the Core Facilitator must always conduct an independent assessment of the justification for, and security risks associated with" them. The people whose work is simplified by the cleanup cannot be the only ones judging that it is safe.
description: Defined by exclusion — no risk-parameter modifications, no new protocol elements — and admitted only after a rationale post and written technical confirmation from the lead Spell team.
